current.text: He has a calf strain, his fourth calf strain in 12 months. He missed the preseason and Yahoo lists him as questionable.
He will probably miss the start of the season.
He re-signed with Charlotte for 3 years and 74 million and is the projected starting point guard.
Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges. The roster has no backup point guard the team trusts.
When healthy he should play about 30 to 32 minutes, up about 7 from last season. Dennis Schroder is not expected to cut into his minutes.
His usage should stay high, about 28 percent, but dip a little from last season's level. He shares the ball with Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller and could be the third or fourth usage option.
In the bigger role he could average 20 or more points and about 5 to 7 assists.
His free throw percentage should bounce back after last season's drop.
Because of the calf, experts now push him into the 90s or later. Pick 84 is too early, and one expert no longer targets him. Healthy, they would take him about 20 spots higher, in the 60s and 70s.
In one auction mock after the injury news, 13 USD was called really good value.

Charlotte has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum. Its playoff schedule is 4-3-4 games for a March 28 end. The two-game week is the matchup starting March 1. One expert believes the two-game week falls in the playoffs.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take many threes. Playmaking will be spread across several players.
Charlotte projects as a play-in team.

durable.text: He helps in points, threes and free throws.
He is a streaky, inconsistent shooter, and his FG% swings up and down.
He has a big enough sample to count as a good shooter, including off the dribble.
He gets into the paint, finishes at the rim and gets to the free throw line.
He is a fine passer but not a pass-first point guard.
His steals and blocks are very poor. He has one of the worst combined steals and blocks numbers for a starter.
Calf strains keep coming back, so more missed games are a risk.

note: Healthy, experts saw him as a 60s to 70s player, with about 20 points, close to 3 threes and good FT%, as the starting point guard. A fourth calf strain in 12 months pushes him into the 90s. Our league paid 15 USD last season, but Yahoo values him at 9 USD and ESPN at 2 USD. That makes him a mid-range bid of about 5 to 10 USD for builds that want points, threes and FT% and can absorb weak steals, blocks and turnovers. Early in the season, check when he returns from the calf, whether he gets the 30-plus minutes, and whether his FG% holds up.
